task: retained graph CPU-sample profile at frozen source; no source edits

sampling.lost_samples: recorded per profile; zero is no loss reported

filtering: For each capture, retain samples whose TGID is one of the benchmark executable TGIDs and whose comm is either that executable (15-character kernel-truncated name) or a GC-marker/marker comm. This keeps the benchmark process’s libc and kernel callchain frames, plus any marker-thread samples in its TGID, while excluding Python pre-exec samples even when they share the child TGID and excluding the Python/perf launcher TGID. All retained TIDs equaled TGID in these captures; no secondary-thread or marker-comm samples were observed (this does not establish that the program cannot create threads).
cpu_interpretation: CPU sample shares, not wall-clock shares. Profiles ran sequentially with no other benchmark jobs. Sample-level elapsed_seconds are captured under perf and are provenance only, not timing claims.

build.translation_units: separate C translation units; no LTO

tool_limitations: perf annotate on custom_AS-list symbol new_old terminated with exit 139 (segmentation fault) on this host; perf record, perf script, and perf report resolved stacks and symbols normally. This is an external profiler-tool limitation, not a Medaka defect.
